content:
alex: Heads-up — customer reported stream abort mid-request when switching networks (5G -> home WiFi). They saw a partial JSON chunk, client retried and ended up billed for full response twice. Repro steps below.

sam: Which SDK + version? any client logs?

maya: Device/OS, and are they using our JS or mobile SDK?

alex: Android 13, redwood-client v0.8.2 (mobile). Long completion (~40s). Client code uses SSE via our mobile SDK. Attaching minimal repro and snippets below.

ingest-bot: ingest-bot: created ticket #SUP-12345 from email report (priority: high)

alex: Repro steps I used locally:
1) Start a streaming completion that emits tokens for >30s.
2) While stream is active toggle mobile data off then back on (simulate carrier->wifi).
3) Client reconnects and triggers a new request without an idempotency key.

Minimal curl (non-SDK repro):
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream?model=rm-large&prompt=long_workload"
```

Mobile SDK snippet (pseudo):
```js
const stream = client.stream({model: 'rm-large', prompt, stream: true});
stream.on('data', chunk => render(chunk));
// toggle airplane mode mid-stream -> socket FIN observed
```

Server logs I pulled (sanitized):
```
[3041592600] frontend: client_closed 499 reqid=abcd1234 src_ip=10.1.2.3
[3041592602] worker: start reqid=abcd1234 conn=worker-7 model=rm-large
[3041592695] worker: finish 200 reqid=abcd1234 tokens=234
```

jordan: Two quick ones — is this only for SSE or also websocket? Are they using any resume/offset on the client? Also check token TTL/rotation.

alex: It's SSE in this case. Token TTL is 5m and the request is under TTL, so no token refresh mid-request. We see socket FIN from client at network switch then a fresh connection that issues the same logical request from the app. Client does not send an idempotency key. Logs show frontend 499 followed by worker 200 on retry.

maya: Can you grep for 499/duplicate reqid patterns across service for other customers? If widespread, it's a runtime bug.

alex: Quick grep shows ~12 similar sequences in the last 72h, most mobile carriers. Sample: frontend 499 reqid=ef56..., then worker 200 reqid=ef56... (same reqid reused by client).

sam: Short-term ask to customer: enable SDK debug, send HAR/pcap if possible, and try with the JS SDK (desktop) to isolate mobile connectivity. Long-term: we should add server-side dedupe on idempotency key or require client-generated request-id for streaming requests. Also consider marking 499-triggered retries as potential duplicates for billing.

support-bot: support-bot: escalation labeled "eng-runtime" and assigned to @eng-runtime, tag added: billing-review

jordan: I'll pick this up for triage. If logs confirm duplicate billing tokens were counted, we should prepare a one-off credit and PR to add dedupe logic. @finance FYI.

alex: Thanks — I'll ask the customer for HAR + SDK logs and test with a small code change to generate an idempotency header on client retries. Will update ticket #SUP-12345 with attachments. :thumbsup:
